newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher, bolstered by natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher, bolstered by natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Tuesday, bolstered by strength in natural gas futures amid extreme cold covering the continental U.S.
"It's basically gas and strong power prices," said an East Coast broker.
"It's just short-covering," a Houston power marketer said.
February natgas to the San Juan/Blanco Hub in New Mexico finished the day at $3.12-$3.17, up from Monday's $3.05-$3.15.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures finished up 13.9 cents at $3.393 per million British thermal units.
Day-ahead power prices for firm, peak delivery in the West slipped from Monday's highs, but remained firm in the mid-$40 a megawatt hour (MWh) range.
February California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up $1.03 at $15.43 after high a session high of $16.00. March COB ended up 20 cents at $12.60.
February Palo Verde (PV) futures settled 95 cents higher at $17.48 after hitting a high of $18.00. March PV ended at $14.50, unchanged from Monday's settlement.
The 790 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant near Laughlin, Nevada, resumed operation today after being shut early Monday for repairs.
The 750 MW unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired generating station in Page, Ariz., returned to service after tripping off line Monday.

The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear generating unit in Richland, Wash., was operating at full output after production was nearly halved last week to correct a problem with the motor for its adjustable speed drive system.

According to Weather Service Corp, much of the West would remain in extreme chill through mid-week with temperatures running five to 15 Fahrenheit degrees below normal. Precipitation is forecast for California through Thursday while the eastern section of the Southwest would stay dry.
